fields.quoted_span:
The HSNA also requires landlords and foreclosing owners to send a copy of the
Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease, together with a Certificate of
Compliance/Service, to the City of Boston’s Office of Housing Stability
fields.note: The notice duty, the copy to the Office of Housing Stability, non-waiver, enforcement entities, the penalty schedule and the eviction not being halted are all in the document. Not in D014: the City's online portal, the tenant's contact information being sent to the City, and the fine for failing to submit to the portal. Those come from D013.

The document also supports the other elements: the notice served with the Notice to Quit, the copy to the Office of Housing Stability, the first-offense warning, non-waivability, and that a violation DOES NOT halt the eviction process.

fields.quoted_span: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
fields.note: The document gives the October 2020 passage and the November 6, 2020 effective date.

fields.quoted_span: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
fields.note: The document says the ordinance takes effect and describes it as operative. It does not explicitly state its current in-force status, so that is inferred.

fields.quoted_span:
The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
fields.note: The two exemptions (hospital, skilled nursing or health facility; non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility) are listed as the only exempt properties.
The section number 10-11.7 and the name HSNA appear. The document does not say "Boston City Code" and does not mention the alias "ch. 10-11"; it refers only to City of Boston Ordinances.
